text:
B: Afternoon! Gary. You alright, mate?
A: Yeah, hiya. Liam. Sorry, I thought last round were the last one. I'd nearly logged off.
B: Ha, me too, I was halfway to the kettle. Where are you, Liam?
A: Doncaster.
B: Rovers fan, I saw the photo. I'm Walsall, so we're in the same boat, mate. League Two, suffering every Saturday.
A: Oh, right. Yeah. We lost again Saturday. Three on the bounce.
B: We couldn't hit a barn door either. We'll be coming to yours this season, won't we? I might pop up. Not in the away end, mind, I'll see if a customer's got a box.
A: Don't think we've got many boxes, to be honest. It's not that sort of ground.
B: Ha, fair enough. What do you do, then?
A: Er, shelf-stacking. Nights, at a supermarket. Replenishment, they call it.
B: Nights, eh. Don't know how you do it. What's that, full-time?
A: No, twenty-five hours. Four nights. I'd like more, really. Or full-time. They've talked about shift leads, but I don't know. I'm not sure I'd be any good telling people what to do, do you know what I mean?
B: Mate, listen. Half the managers I know couldn't organise a bacon bap from the van. You turn up on time, yeah? You know the job?
A: Yeah. I've never been late. Not once in four years.
B: There you go, that's the hard bit done. The rest is just being decent to the lads and not panicking. I'm going for sales manager myself, regional. Bigger car allowance, which is the main thing, between you and me. You just put yourself forward, you don't wait to be asked. Nobody's going to come and give it you on a plate.
A: Yeah. I suppose. I just get a bit worked up before stuff like that. Meetings and that. Can't sleep.
B: Everyone does. You just don't let them see it.
A: Ha. Maybe. What do you do, then? You sound like a manager already.
B: Senior sales, industrial fixings. Bolts, anchors, threaded rod. I look after the big accounts across the Midlands. On the road most of the week, fifty-odd hours. Keeps me out of the house, Karen'd say.
A: Sounds busy.
B: It is, but you've got the car. That's my office, the 5 Series. What do you do when you're not stacking shelves?
A: Fishing, mostly. Coarse fishing. Ponds, the canal. And FIFA, if I'm honest.
B: Fishing, I never got into it. Golf's mine. Sunday mornings, out Sutton Coldfield way. Same thing really, isn't it, standing about in the countryside hoping for the best.
A: Ha, yeah. Except bait's cheaper than golf, I reckon. Though maggots have gone up a fortune.
B: Everything has, mate. My curry house has put two quid on a balti.
A: I only have a chippy on Fridays. That's gone up an' all.
B: Right, I reckon that's us done. Go for that shift lead job, yeah? Good luck to the Rovers. Except against us.
A: Cheers, Gary. Same to you. Well, not against us.
B: Ha! Tara, mate.
